findings.title: Deleting the cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the old timestamp
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike `disconnectMutation`, which does so in `onSettled`. `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows 'Last updated: …' and offers 'Delete cached data' again. Nothing guarantees `onChanged` refetches, because it is optional and is `props.onChanged` from the wrapper. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess` or `onSettled` of the delete mutation.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`. tRPC maps this to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), so the client and monitoring see a server fault rather than a 403/404. Other tRPC handlers use `TRPCError` with `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND`. Use `TRPCError` here so the response code is correct and error tracking is not flooded with false 500s.

findings.title: No tests for the new delete mutation, repository method, or component
findings.body: The PR adds an ownership-checked destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), handler enrichment with `cacheUpdatedAt`, and a new dropdown component with conditional rendering. It adds no tests for any of them. The ownership check that stops a user deleting another user's cache, and the empty-cache and delegation-credential paths, are the logic most worth covering.

findings.title: Unused SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump adds a DB write to every cache refresh
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an `updateMany` over all of the credential's SelectedCalendar rows. This runs on every webhook-triggered cache refresh and on `unwatchCalendar`. The new UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the write has no consumer. The PR notes already question whether it should be removed. It also depends on Prisma bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty `data: {}`, which is fragile. Remove it, or justify it with a consumer.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId, which nothing uses
findings.body: The `Pick` types for `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, and the select in `user.ts` was extended to match. No code in this PR reads these fields, since the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Widening a shared exported type forces every other producer of `UserWithCalendars` (platform libraries, API v2, tests) to supply the fields or fail type-checking, and it loads extra columns for nothing. Revert unless a consumer is added.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' text uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's UI locale. Users of other locales see US-style dates (M/D/YY, 12-hour) next to translated strings. Use the locale from `useLocale()`, or the existing dayjs/locale formatting helpers, instead of a fixed locale.

findings.title: Unrelated dev script is macOS-only and exits 0 on failure
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` works only with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU sed (Linux) the empty argument is parsed as the script, so the `.env` update fails. `cleanup` ends with `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and 'Failed to extract URL' paths report success. The script rewrites a relative `../.env` that depends on the caller's working directory. It is also unrelated to cache status and actions and is not wired to any package script. Drop it from this PR or fix these problems.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to unpinned `npx tsx`, an undeclared dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` changed from `ts-node` (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`. `tsx` is not declared in this package, so `npx` downloads whatever version is latest at run time. Behaviour is then unpinned and breaks offline. The change is unrelated to this feature. If tsx is wanted, add it as a devDependency and call it directly, or revert.

findings.title: Migration warning contradicts the SQL
findings.body: The header says the column was added 'without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty', but the statement adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. The stale auto-generated warning is misleading. Also, every pre-existing CalendarCache row gets the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so legacy rows will show the deploy time as 'Last updated' rather than when they were actually populated.
